items.stem: An employee asks a question not covered by any retrieved policy passage. What is the correct behaviour?

options.text: State that no policy covers it and escalate to a human owner
options.rationale: Correct: ungrounded answers invent policy; the safe path is to escalate.

options.text: Answer from Claude's general knowledge of similar policies
options.rationale: General knowledge is not this organisation's policy and may be wrong.

options.text: Pick the closest policy and apply it anyway
options.rationale: Applying an unrelated policy misstates the rule.

options.text: Return the longest available policy document
options.rationale: Length is not relevance and does not answer the question.

items.explanation: Correct: ungrounded answers invent policy; the safe path is to escalate.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO practices stop a superseded policy from being served as current? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Marking the current version with explicit status metadata
options.rationale: Correct: status metadata lets retrieval prefer the live version.

options.text: Moving superseded policies out of the retrieval scope
options.rationale: Correct: excluding old versions prevents them being returned.

options.text: Keeping all drafts and finals in one undifferentiated library
options.rationale: Mixing versions is exactly what causes stale answers.

options.text: Relying on file names alone to signal recency
options.rationale: File-name conventions drift and are not reliable status signals.

items.explanation: Correct: status metadata lets retrieval prefer the live version.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: How should a Teams policy answer present itself to stay trustworthy?

options.text: With the cited source and a clear non-authoritative disclaimer
options.rationale: Correct: sources plus a disclaimer let users verify and escalate.

options.text: As a definitive ruling to save the user time
options.rationale: Presenting it as a ruling overstates the assistant's authority.

options.text: Without links, to keep the message short
options.rationale: Hiding sources removes the user's ability to verify.

options.text: Only in a private channel the owner controls
options.rationale: Channel privacy does not address how the answer presents itself.

items.explanation: Correct: sources plus a disclaimer let users verify and escalate.
